post_title: Folded cuffs keeps turning inside out in simulation
post_details: Hopefully someone can give me the reason why this happens (a lot) and what to do to prevent this. For cuffs, but also collars, I've used the Fold Arrangement tool to fold the cuff inside, with Fold Rendering on. Next step is to sew the top and bottom of the cuff to each other, so the cuff is closed. The front of the cuff is blue, the back is white (to make it easy to see the difference). What's so frustrating, is that when I put simulation on and pull on it to straighten things out (or, it also happens when I superimpose something under), the cuffs flips inside out very slow. What am I missing here or doing wrong?

comments.comment_body: Forgot to mention... The sewline of the top to the bottom of the cuff has been set to a Turned Seam. It just looks like if you pull too hard on the fabric, the whole thing turns inside out.

Thanks again jne4sl! Didn't know that option either. I'll try it and if it still doesn't work like I want to, I'll try a trick I saw on youtube (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dIzd_-QpTvY&ampfeature=youtu.be) make halve of the cuff and double it up with layer clone under. Have a great weekend!

Hi 422301299813. I would suggest Strengthening the cuffs before folding/rendering them. Once they have settled in the render then remove strengthening. This should help to keep the right side of the fabric on the outside

Yes, layer clone is good, but I'm usually working with an existing pattern, and I'd like to use it as-is whenever possible. Sewing lines default to "Front", which is why many people only layer things front on top of front. If you then flip the normal of the under layer, the sewing line is flipped appropriately, too, so it works even if you're unaware of that detail.

Thanks 408464537934 for the tip about strenghtening. That's what I usually do when I fold the first time and it works like a charm. It's just that sometimes when I have to place something in the same area it starts to act up. 424140880473 I understand that you would want to use the pattern as best as possible. My goal is a bit different since I'm more focused on the presentation and the garment looking as perfect as possible. If I have to tweak the pattern a bit to make it so, than that's what I'll do -)
424140880473 Using a single layer and simulating the thickness and edge is exactly what I've done now, and it looks good in my opinion. And with a lot less frustration. Thanks for your advice!

Yeah, but then you might be better off using a single layer and simulating the thickness and edge, as opposed to hiding the seam you've introduced along the fold by layering. There's always a tradeoff or at least a choice to deliberate. If you're getting mesh rot along a seam, not the fold, force the sublayer of the sewing line to fix it. Along a fold you might need to strengthen/re-drape.

In addition to turned seam, click "Set Sublayer" to on, and chose Sublayer "Back". You want this edge sewn to the *back* of the other edge. Ignore "Reverse Direction" because in your case the seam is sewn back to back and direction doesn't matter. (If ever you are sewing right side to wrong side, you might need to watch the direction, too. It's also depicted by an arrowhead on the line connecting the sewn segments.) This helps a lot, but it's still possible for layers of mesh to get entangled, especially near the fold.

post_title: Flip Topstitch, show the back of the topstitch on the front
post_details: For a project I have a t-shirt to re-create in Clo. The actual t-shirt I have in front of me, so I can check how everything has been made. This t-shirt has a necktape that also runs under the shoulder seams. It looks like the Library-topstitch ISO_401_Chainstitch.sst has been used to sew this necktape to the collar and back-yoke. Is there a way that I can 'flip' this topstitch, so that what now is the back of the stitch, will be the front of the stitch?

comments.comment_body: Yes, when you open this topstitch in the property editor, there are tabs 1 and 2 for the two stitches. By default 1 is on Face is front only, and 2 Face is on back only (scroll to the very bottom under Configuration). Swap these settings. You may need to copy the topstitch, so you can use the original configuration, too.
Thank you jne4sl! I've tried that option, but didn't go that extra step to change it in both tabs so they're opposite of each other :-)

post_title: How to add  binding finishing to Cuff slit
post_details: Hi Everyone , Could someone help me replicate a binding finishing at cuff vent/slit ... please see below pic for reference

comments.comment_body: This is sewn by apply a bias binding to a slash. At the ends near the cuff, the seam allowance is binding width, but tapers to a minimum near the end of the slash. The inside fold of the binding is sewn shut with a small diagonal line, this is hidden inside the sleeve. So, mark a slash and essentially cut away a dart of binding width around that. Create a strip twice the length of the dart. This can be simulated with a strip of single width, or constructed with a strip of double width with a fold. I did the double layer. The key to getting things to fall into position is setting fold angles, and setting sublayers for some of the sewing. I replaced the tower placket in the supplied dress shirt with the simplified placket.

post_title: Edit motion files, use half the animation or add transition in the middle
post_details: Is there a way to edit the animations in clo? I only want to use the second half of a catwalk animation so that the model is walking away but I need it to transition from a pose into that walk so I can't just render the second half. I tried saving the joint motion of the play region but it didn't work. Surely there is a simple way to cut the first half of the animation off.

comments.comment_body: Hi 419070450053. If you only want to render out a single part of the animation you can do that. When in the Render Engine go into Image/Video Properties change Region from "Entire Region" to "Play Region". You can then set the Start/End frames to the section of the animation that you want to render.

Hi 419070450053 , I guess I'm late but maybe my response would be helpful for other CLO3D users! There is a way you can ''cut your animation'' using the following steps: -Record the animation as is normally done. -Choose the step (frame) you want your final animation to start -Change start to the desired frame -Record again the animation (this new one will start directly from the selected frame) -This way you will create an animation track with the desired length as you can see in the picture. -Finally delete de transition and the first recording track. If someone needs more explanation on this I will share more screenshots or whatever :)
